# pve_user (Resource)

Manages a PVE user account (`/access/users/{userid}`). The account lives in the realm encoded in `userid`; the realm itself must already exist. Password changes after create go through PVE's separate password endpoint, which this resource does not model.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Manage a PVE user account in the `pve` realm.
resource "pve_user" "ci" {
  userid    = "ci@pve"
  comment   = "CI automation account"
  email     = "ci@example.com"
  firstname = "CI"
  lastname  = "Bot"
  enable    = true
  expire    = 0

  groups = ["ops"]

  # Only sent at create; PVE returns the secret-free response and never
  # allows reading the password back.
  password = var.ci_password
}

variable "ci_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `userid` (String) Full User ID in `name@realm` format, e.g. `root@pam` or `ci@pve`. Changing this forces replacement.

### Optional

- `comment` (String) Free-form comment, up to 2048 characters.
- `email` (String) Email address, up to 254 characters.
- `enable` (Boolean) Enable the account. Defaults to `true`; set `false` to disable login.
- `expire` (Number) Account expiration date (seconds since epoch). `0` means no expiration date. Must be 0 or greater.
- `firstname` (String) First name, up to 1024 characters.
- `groups` (Set of String) Set of PVE group IDs the user belongs to. The groups themselves are managed by `pve_group`; removing every entry here removes the user from all groups.
- `keys` (String) Keys for two factor auth (yubico): up to 4096 characters of `[0-9a-zA-Z!=]`.
- `lastname` (String) Last name, up to 1024 characters.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Initial password (8 to 64 characters). Only sent at create; PVE manages later password changes through its own password endpoint, so changes to this attribute after create have no effect.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
#!/bin/sh
# Import a PVE user by its full user ID.
terraform import pve_user.ci "root@pam"
```
